question_text: A new law is passed that prohibits the publication of any news article critical of the government. A group of journalists challenges the law's constitutionality. Which of the following best describes the power of the Supreme Court to review this law?

options.text: The Supreme Court can declare the law unconstitutional if it finds that it violates the freedom of the press, which is protected by the Constitution.
The Supreme Court cannot review the law because it is a political question that only Congress can decide.
The Supreme Court can review the law only if the President requests an advisory opinion.
The Supreme Court can review the law but only after it has been enforced for at least one year.
